title: Female borrowers who include explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about children's ages or education may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who describe animal-related businesses, such as pig or fish breeding, may fund faster.
Pitches from men that describe specific operational details, such as door-to-door sales or specific repair materials, tend to decelerate funding.
Female borrowers who use positive descriptive adjectives like 'dynamic' or 'hardworking' may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention owning their own home may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly mention their husband's income or business partnership may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention operating their business from or near the home may fund faster.
Female borrowers who include explicit thanks to lenders may fund faster.
Providing specific demographic details about children, such as number and schooling status, predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayments predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Mentioning local currency amounts or specific institutional affiliations predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
